newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisseki House becomes top gainer on TSE.
newsitem.headline: Nisseki House becomes top gainer on TSE.

text.p: Shares of Nisseki House Industry Co Ltd became the biggest percentage gainer on Monday morning, following news that it had dismissed its missing president and would issue 9.65 billion yen worth of shares to third parties, brokers said.
Nisseki House was up 50 yen, or 24.63 percent, at 253 by 0153 GMT. Its shares are listed on the first section of the exchange.

The company said on Friday that it would issue 9.65 billion yen worth of shares to Kotobuki Industry Co Ltd, to three other firms and to three individuals on January 31 to improve its financial stability.

The company also announced on Friday that it had dismissed its missing president Saburo Horiuchi. It said that the last time it was in contact with Horiuchi was on December 11. Nisseki said it did not know what had happened to Horiuchi.
Nisseki also revised downward its earnings forecast for the year ending March 31 due to intensifying price competition.

Nisseki House now expects 1996/97 sales to total 61 billion yen, down from the 69 billion yen it previously forecast in November. It expects a parent current loss of 9.1 billion, compared with a previous forecast of 1.6 billion yen.
